llm.summary: The skill is coherent as a VMware audit and policy helper, but it needs review because its policy controls can fail open or be bypassed with a simple environment variable.

dimensions.detail: For a security-control component, the documented default allow behavior without rules, global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED bypass, and silent allow-all mode when PyYAML is missing are under-scoped for high-impact VMware operations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a uv package and the skill says it is auto-installed as a dependency of VMware skills; the reviewed artifact contains documentation only, not package source code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Auto-loading across the VMware skill family is clearly disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it gives this dependency broad influence over many wrapped tools.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Local persistence to ~/.vmware/audit.db and ~/.vmware/rules.yaml is disclosed, includes rotation and permission guidance, and the artifact says no credentials are logged or sent externally.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifact: it provides audit logging, policy checks, input sanitization, and a wrapper used by other VMware skills rather than exposing its own MCP tools.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with local audit logging under ~/.vmware and you will actively configure rules. In production, create and protect ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, monitor for ok_bypassed events, restrict use of VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED, and verify PyYAML is installed so policy enforcement is actually active.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Broad dependency activation is expected for an infrastructure wrapper and is disclosed in the skill, so this is a scope note rather than the main reason for review.
[SQP-2] expected: Exporting audit logs is expected for compliance workflows, but users should treat exported records as sensitive operational data.
[SQP-2] expected: Recording agent, workflow, and OS user metadata is disclosed and fits audit logging, though it has privacy implications in shared environments.
[SQP-2] unexpected: A single environment variable that bypasses all policy checks is a material concern for a policy-enforcement layer used across many tools.
[SQP-2] expected: Bulk JSON export is purpose-aligned, but the documentation should warn more clearly about handling those logs confidentially.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The CLI reference normalizes the policy bypass without strong break-glass scoping or authorization guidance.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Allowing all operations when no rules file exists is documented, but it creates a fail-open deployment posture for a security component.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Silently allowing all operations when PyYAML is missing materially weakens enforcement and could surprise operators.
